'''Anna Parker Fessenden''' (April 8, 1896 – May 3, 1972) was an American botanist and mathematics educator.

== Early life and education ==
Anna Parker Fessenden was born in [[Thomaston, Maine]], and raised in [[Mattapan|Mattapan, Massachusetts]], the middle of three daughters of William S. Fessenden and Alida Mary Mehan Fessenden.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|date=1972-05-04|title=Noted Math and Science Teacher Dies in Camden|pages=24|work=The Bangor Daily News|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/87907076/noted-math-and-science-teacher-dies-in/|access-date=2021-10-28|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> Her mother was assistant principal of [[Sandwich High School]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=1920-06-13|title=Sandwich High Alumni to Meet|pages=55|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93349386/sandwich-high-alumni-to-meet/|access-date=2022-01-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

Fessenden graduated from [[Boston Latin Academy|Girls' Latin School]] in 1914,<ref>{{Cite news|date=1913-05-01|title=Girls Present 'Iphigenia'|pages=16|work=Boston Evening Transcript|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93346223/girls-present-iphigenia/|access-date=2022-01-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1914-06-19|title=Girls' Latin High|pages=10|work=Boston Evening Transcript|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93346544/girls-latin-high/|access-date=2022-01-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and graduated from [[Smith College]] in 1918.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Smith College|url=https://archive.org/details/class1918smit/page/36/mode/2up?q=Fessenden|title=Class of 1918|year=1918|pages=51|publisher = Smith College|via=Internet Archive}}</ref> As a college student, she was active in the Smith College [[Unitarian Universalism|Unitarian]] Club,<ref>{{Cite news|date=1916-06-19|title=New England Girls Chosen|pages=13|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93346318/new-england-girls-chosen/|access-date=2022-01-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and she edited and wrote for the ''Smith College Monthly''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Fessenden|first=Anna Parker|date=January 1918|title=The Beacon|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DHEUAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA176|journal=Smith College Monthly|volume=25|pages=176–177}}</ref> She earned a master's degree from the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1920.<ref name=":0" /> Her master's thesis, under advisor [[Josephine Tilden]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Horsfield|first=Margaret|date=June 13, 2016|title=The Enduring Legacy of Josephine Tilden|url=https://www.hakaimagazine.com/features/enduring-legacy-josephine-tilden/|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-28|website=Hakai Magazine|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181205173915/https://www.hakaimagazine.com/features/enduring-legacy-josephine-tilden/ |archive-date=2018-12-05 }}</ref> was titled "Observations on Two Rare Australian Algae, ''Myriocladia Sciurus'', Harvey and ''Bactrophora Irregularis'', N. SP."<ref>Fessenden, Anna Parker. [https://conservancy.umn.edu/bitstream/handle/11299/179463/una-theses-0526.pdf?sequence=1 "Observations on Two Rare Australian Algae, Myriocladia Sciurus, Harvey and Bactrophora Irregularis, N. SP."] (1920).</ref>

== Career ==
Fessenden taught botany at [[Vassar College]],<ref>{{Cite book|last=College|first=Vassar|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CkoWAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA11|title=General Catalogue of the Officers and Graduates of Vassar College, Poughkeepsie, New York|date=1920|pages=11|language=en}}</ref> [[Wellesley College]]<ref>{{Cite book|last=College|first=Wellesley|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HmcZAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA63|title=Annual Reports [of] President and Treasurer|date=1921|pages=63|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=1920-10-05|title=Reception Held at Wellesley College|pages=2|work=The Boston Globe|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/93346451/reception-held-at-wellesley-college/|access-date=2022-01-24|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref> and at the University of Minnesota.<ref>{{Cite book|last=University of Minnesota|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZnogAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA59|title=Bulletin|date=1922|publisher=|pages=59|language=en}}</ref> She and Josephine Tilden co-authored a 22-page article on [[brown algae]] from Australia.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Tilden|first1=Josephine E.|last2=Fessenden|first2=Anna Parker|date=1930|title=Bactrophora irregularis, a New Brown Alga from Australia|url=https://doi.org/10.2307/2480641|journal=Bulletin of the Torrey Botanical Club|volume=57|issue=6|pages=381–388|doi=10.2307/2480641|jstor=2480641|url-access=subscription}}</ref> She taught mathematics at [[Needham High School]] in Massachusetts for 36 years, and was a director of math programs for the Needham school district. She retired from teaching in 1962.<ref name=":0" />

Fessenden was an active member of several clubs including the [[Audubon|Audubon Society]], and a trustee of the Thomaston Historical Society.<ref name=":0" />

{{Botanist|Fess.|inline=yes}}

== Personal life ==
Fessenden died in 1972, aged 76 years, in [[Camden, Maine]]. Her grave is with her parents' graves, in [[Sandwich, Massachusetts]].<ref name=":0" />
